questions.title: Super No Parens Behavior
questions.description: What does `super` (without parentheses) do inside an overridden method?
questions.Option1: Calls the parent class version of the same method, forwarding the current method's arguments
questions.Option2: Skips the parent method and returns nil

questions.title: Private Method Accessibility
questions.description: From where can a private instance method be called in Ruby?
questions.Option1: From anywhere with an explicit receiver
questions.Option2: Only from within the same class instance, without an explicit receiver

questions.title: Single Inheritance Definition
questions.description: What does 'single inheritance' mean in Ruby?
questions.Option1: A class can have multiple parent classes
questions.Option2: A class can have exactly one direct superclass
questions.Option3: Only one method can be overridden per class
questions.Option4: Only one instance can exist at a time

questions.title: Super Empty Parens Behavior
questions.description: What does `super()` (with empty parentheses) do?
questions.Option1: Calls the parent method passing no arguments
questions.Option2: Calls the parent method passing all current arguments

questions.title: Override Prints Subclass Message
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class A
  def greet; "Hello from A"; end
end
class B < A
  def greet; "Hello from B"; end
end
puts B.new.greet

questions.title: Super Multiplies Value
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class A
  def initialize; @x = 10; end
  def x; @x; end
end
class B < A
  def x; super * 2; end
end
puts B.new.x

questions.title: Counter Class Method Output
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class Counter
  @@n = 0
  def initialize; @@n += 1; end
  def self.n; @@n; end
end
Counter.new
Counter.new
Counter.new
puts Counter.n

questions.title: Super Passing Argument
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class A
  def m(x); "A:#{x}"; end
end
class B < A
  def m(x); super(x) + " B:#{x}"; end
end
puts B.new.m(5)

questions.title: Private Method Called Internally
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class C
  def call_me; secret; end
  private
  def secret; "hidden"; end
end
puts C.new.call_me

questions.title: Protected Cross Instance Compare
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class Box
  def initialize(v); @v = v; end
  def bigger?(other); v > other.v; end
  protected
  def v; @v; end
end
a = Box.new(5)
b = Box.new(3)
puts a.bigger?(b)

questions.title: Private Vs Protected Difference
questions.description: What is the key difference between private and protected methods in Ruby?
questions.Option1: Private methods are inherited, protected are not
questions.Option2: Private methods can only be called without an explicit receiver; protected methods can be called on other instances of the same class
questions.Option3: Protected methods run faster than private methods

questions.title: Class Variable Shared With Subclass
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class Base
  @@count = 0
  def initialize; @@count += 1; end
  def self.count; @@count; end
end
class Derived < Base
  def initialize; super; end
end
Base.new
Derived.new
Derived.new
puts Base.count

questions.title: Method Resolution With Super
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class P
  def who; "P"; end
end
class Q < P
  def who; "Q-#{super}"; end
end
puts Q.new.who

questions.title: Super Forwards Argument Value
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:

  def m(x = 1); "A#{x}"; end
end
class B < A
  def m(x = 1); super + "B#{x}"; end

questions.title: Method Visibility Chained Call
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class T
  def a; "a"; end
  def b; "b" + c; end
  private
  def c; "c"; end
  protected
  def d; "d"; end
end

puts t.b

questions.title: Class Variable Sharing Hierarchy
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class Counter
  @@n = 0
  def self.inc; @@n += 1; end
  def self.n; @@n; end
end
class Sub < Counter; end
Sub.inc
Counter.inc
Sub.inc
puts Sub.n

questions.title: Super Forwards Splat Args
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class A
  def m(*args); args.sum; end
end
class B < A
  def m(*args); super; end
end
puts B.new.m(1, 2, 3, 4)
